source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 22 decembrie — «Sfânta Mare Muceniță Anastasia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ας Δεκεμβρίου — «Αγία Αναστασία η Μεγαλομάρτυς η Φαρμακολύτρια»

attestations.note: The life page `/3239/` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps for the Romanian, and it is the same woman: the great-martyr of Rome under Diocletian whom the Greek calls Φαρμακολύτρια, the loosener of poisons. The page names her father Praetextatus, a Roman patrician, her mother Fausta, and her husband Poplios, a ruler of the Romans and a fanatical idolater; it gives the by-name its own explanation, that she dressed poorly and carried food and money into the prisons. Its head gives «(; - 290)» and its last line «παρέδωσε το πνεύμα της στην πυρά το 290 μ.Χ.», so a `dates` object is drafted where the folder had none. It names the places of her relics — part of the skull at Koutloumousiou on Athos, part of the skull and one foot at the monastery of her name at Vasilika of Thessaloniki, a finger with flesh at Pantokrator on Athos, a hand at Panachrantou on Andros, a portion of the right hand at Kykkos in Cyprus — which is not drafted. Rome is named as her origin and no coordinate is proposed. An apolytikion and a kontakion are printed with their ἦχος and their automela, both naming her, and both are taken; the Οἶκος and the Κάθισμα are kinds the schema does not hold and are left out. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (28 September 2026).

hymns.text: Mieluşeaua Ta, Iisuse, Anastasia, strigă cu glas mare: pe Tine, Mirele meu, te iubesc și pe Tine căutându-Te mă chinuiesc și împreună mă răstignesc și împreună mă îngrop cu Botezul Tău; și pătimesc pentru Tine, ca să împărățesc întru Tine; și mor pentru tine, ca să viez pentru Tine; ci, ca o jertfă fără de prihană, primește-mă pe mine ceea ce cu dragoste mă jertfesc Ție. Pentru rugăciunile ei, ca un Milostiv, mântuiește sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfintei Mari Mucenițe Anastasia, glasul 4 (the common of a woman martyr, printed with her name in it)

english.text: Your ewe-lamb, Jesus, Anastasia, cries out with a loud voice: you, my Bridegroom, I love, and seeking you I suffer, and I am crucified with you and buried with you in your Baptism; and I suffer for you, that I may reign in you; and I die for you, that I may live for you. But receive me, as a sacrifice without blemish, who sacrifice myself to you in love. At her prayers, as the Merciful One, save our souls.

hymns.text: Tῶν μαρτύρων ταῖς χρείαις διακονήσασα, μαρτυρικῶς ἐμιμήσω τὰς ἀριστείας αὐτῶν, δι' ἀθλήσεως ἐχθρὸν καταπαλαίσασα· ὅθεν βλαστάνεις δαψιλῶς χάριν ἄφθονον ἀεί, θέοφρων Ἀναστασία, τοῖς προσιοῦσιν ἐκ πόθου τῇ ἀρωγῇ τῆς προστασίας σου.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον — the first hymn on the page of «Αγία Αναστασία η Μεγαλομάρτυς η Φαρμακολύτρια», and it names her. Copied as printed: the site sets the first letter as a Latin capital T, which is its markup and not a reading.

english.text: Having served the martyrs in their needs, you imitated their deeds of valour in your own martyrdom, throwing down the enemy by your contest; and so you put forth abundant and unstinted grace for ever upon those who come with longing to the help of your protection, God-minded Anastasia.

hymns.text: Οἱ ἐν πειρασμοῖς, καὶ θλίψεσιν ὑπάρχοντες, πρὸς τὸν σὸν ναόν, προστρέχοντες λαμβάνουσι, τὰ σεπτὰ δωρήματα, τῆς ἔν σοὶ ἐνοικούσης θείας χάριτος Ἀναστασία· σὺ γὰρ ἀεί, τῷ κόσμῳ πηγάζεις τὰ ἰάματα.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — on the page of «Αγία Αναστασία η Μεγαλομάρτυς η Φαρμακολύτρια», printed as hers and naming her.

english.text: Those who are in trials and afflictions, running to your church, receive the venerable gifts of the divine grace that dwells in you, Anastasia; for you pour out healings upon the world for ever.

death.note: saint.gr: «Τελικά η αγία Αναστασία παρέδωσε το πνεύμα της στην πυρά το 290 μ.Χ.», with the page's head «(; - 290)». No year of birth is given; the page says only that she married young. The folder held no `dates` before this.
